title: American Cement Association calls for ‘level playing field’ against imports
summary: American Cement Association calls for ‘level playing field’ against imports
body_markdown:
**US:** ACA president and CEO Diane Tomb published a column addressing the threat of imports ‘at prices US producers struggle to match’ on the US Congress’ The Floor is Yours online noticeboard on 23 November 2026. In the column, Tomb reported 84% growth in imports of cement and clinker into the US over an eight-year period, up to 24.6Mt in 2025. She named Algeria, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Thailand, Türkiye, the UAE and Vietnam as leading import partners by volume. According to Tomb, these countries’ cement industries may receive subsidisation to help ‘prop up overcapacity’ and may not be subject to the same environmental and labour rules as US plants. This places the domestic sector at a disadvantage, endangering livelihoods. “When a plant idles, the whole community feels it,” she said.


Tomb said that the ACA recognises the necessity of cement imports to help meet the US’ infrastructure needs. She said that ‘fair trade and strong domestic industry are compatible’ through a realignment towards ‘trading partners with comparable environmental and labour standards.’ Tomb proposed two tools by which the government can achieve this.


Firstly, Tomb encouraged the US Trade Representative to conclude its Section 301 investigation into foreign subsidisation of cement, among other industries, and to impose tariffs according to its findings. Secondly, she called on President Trump to recognise cement as critical to national security by executive order. This would facilitate favourable treatment in federal procurement, accelerate plant permitting procedures and extend additional support to employees.
